# Data Processing Addendum — Summary

Plain-language summary of the Data Processing Addendum (DPA) attached to every Acme Digital master services agreement signed since January 2026. If this summary and the signed DPA differ, the signed DPA prevails. Questions go to Nicolás Ferraro (IT and Security) or legal@acme.example.

## Roles and scope

The client is the data controller and Acme Digital acts as the data processor: we process personal data only on the client's documented instructions and only to deliver the contracted services (media buying, CRM and email campaigns, analytics and e-commerce operations). The DPA follows Argentina's Personal Data Protection Law 25.326 and, for clients outside Argentina, the data protection law of the client's country.

## Categories of personal data

- Customer contact data (name, email, phone, city), used for audience uploads and always hashed with SHA-256 before it reaches an ad platform.
- Lead data from forms: name, company, role, email, phone and form answers.
- Online identifiers and behavioral data collected by pixels and tags: cookie IDs, device IDs, pages viewed and events.
- Order data from e-commerce platforms: order ID, products, amount and shipping city; never full card numbers.
- Excluded: health data, biometric data and data of children under 13. Processing health data requires a separate annex signed by both parties.

## Subprocessors

Acme currently uses four subprocessors: Litware, Proseware, Trey Research and Wide World Logística.

| Subprocessor | Service | Data involved |
|---|---|---|
| Litware | Litware Vault, storage of access credentials | Access details for client platforms |
| Proseware | Proseware CRM, lead and pipeline management | Lead data |
| Trey Research | Surveys and panels for market research projects | Contact data of survey respondents |
| Wide World Logística | Fulfillment and delivery for e-commerce operations run by Acme | Buyer name, address and phone |

Acme gives clients 30 days' written notice before adding or replacing a subprocessor, and the client may object within that period on reasonable data protection grounds.

## Retention after contract end

Within 30 days after the contract ends, Acme returns the client's personal data (as a CSV export or a platform transfer) and then deletes it from active systems. Backups are purged within 90 days. Acme may keep aggregated, anonymized performance data for benchmarks, and keeps the signed contract and invoices for 10 years as tax rules require.

## Breach notification

Acme notifies the client without undue delay and no later than 48 hours after becoming aware of a personal data breach affecting the client's data. The notice covers what happened, the data categories and approximate number of people affected, likely consequences, the measures taken and a contact person. Updates follow at least every 24 hours until the breach is contained.

## Data location and transfers

Client personal data is stored in Acme's Google Workspace tenant and in the ad and analytics platforms themselves; Acme keeps no copies on personal devices or USB drives. Part of the data is stored in the United States. International transfers rely on the model contract clauses approved by Argentina's data protection authority (AAIP) and, where required, on the standard contractual clauses of the client's jurisdiction.

## Audit rights

The client may audit Acme's compliance once per calendar year, with 30 days' written notice, during business hours and at its own cost. Acme can first answer a security questionnaire and share existing reports; an on-site visit is available after a confirmed breach or when the questionnaire answers are not enough. Auditors sign an NDA before the visit.
